Messages.Author: Shevaun Frazier
Messages.Body:
I had my last tournament last weekend, and a number of questions came up.
Most were pretty simple, but I promised the players (esp. ones who haven't
played in tournaments for a while) that I would ask a few questions.

1) Can Environmental damage be prevented by normal fortitude cards? E.g.
Weather Control vs. Skin of Rock

2) Can normal fortitude cards prevent aggravated damage? E.g. Skin of Rock
vs. a flamethrower

3) In the case of the gangrel Stanislava, what is the definition of
opposing- importantly, when does it start? E.g. Stanislava vs. Raptor- does
the vamp get the intercept?

Thanks, I know some of this is really simple but I did promise

Yours til the sun rises,
Prince Shevy of Edinburgh

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Shevaun Frazier wrote:
> 1) Can Environmental damage be prevented by normal fortitude cards? E.g.
> Weather Control vs. Skin of Rock

Yes.
Unless, of course, the damage is unpreventable. Like Weather Control (card text).

> 2) Can normal fortitude cards prevent aggravated damage? E.g. Skin of Rock
> vs. a flamethrower

Yes.

> 3) In the case of the gangrel Stanislava, what is the definition of
> opposing- importantly, when does it start? E.g. Stanislava vs. Raptor- does
> the vamp get the intercept?

Minions only oppose one another in combat.
The Raptor still provides intercept.

Assuming that Stanislava had enough stealth that the Raptor was
needed to block before, that is. If she was just taking a 0-
stealth action, the Raptor's intercept was superfluous before and
Form of Mist would still be playable by Stanislava for stealth.

Which I'm sure you know, just for the benefit of anyone who might
become confused. :-)
